E3216

Foreign boundary evidence is invalid for {subject}.

What

Foreign boundary evidence is invalid for {subject}.

Why

{reason}.

Fix

{fix}.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E3216: tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.stderr.

Error [E0065]: This function uses the retired `::` body marker.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:7:45
    |
  7 | fn Incrementer.apply(self, x: I32) -[]> I32 :: x + 1
    |                                             ^^
 Why: Named function bodies use braces. `::` binds a name, and `=` fills a slot inside a definition.
 Fix: Replace `::` with `{ … }`; `jet fmt` applies this fix.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0065

Error [E0068]: This callable puts the return type before the arrow.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:10:25
    |
 10 |     fn call(cb: fn(I32) I32 -[]>, x: I32) I32 = "call"
    |                         ^^^
 Why: A return type follows the one arrow: `fn name(...) -> Type { … }`. An effect ceiling splits that arrow: `fn name(...) -[Effects]> Type { … }`.
 Fix: Write `fn name(...) -> Type { … }`, or `fn name(...) -[Effects]> Type { … }`.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0068

Error [E0068]: This callable puts the return type before the arrow.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:10:43
    |
 10 |     fn call(cb: fn(I32) I32 -[]>, x: I32) I32 = "call"
    |                                           ^^^
 Why: A return type follows the one arrow: `fn name(...) -> Type { … }`. An effect ceiling splits that arrow: `fn name(...) -[Effects]> Type { … }`.
 Fix: Write `fn name(...) -> Type { … }`, or `fn name(...) -[Effects]> Type { … }`.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0068

Error [E0302]: `Incrementer` has no field `apply`
  --> cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:15:22
    |
 15 |     print(c.call(inc.apply, 1))
    |                      ^^^^^
 Why: Field access only works on names declared in the struct
 Fix: Check the field names on `Incrementer`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0302

Error [E3216]: Foreign boundary evidence is invalid for managed callback `fn(I32) -[]> I32`.
  --> cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:15:22
    |
 15 |     print(c.call(inc.apply, 1))
    |                      ^^^^^
 Why: Safe foreign callbacks require retained captures, vetted thread entry, explicit completion, consuming ownership, native-access release, and the canonical FFI.C + IO.Write effects.
 Fix: Regenerate the binding from the exact callback plan, or keep the callback capture-free and use the ordinary C callback subset.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3216
